```kql
// Download-and-Execute: curl/wget staging a script in /tmp followed by shell execution
let DownloadToStaging = DeviceProcess
| where FileName in~ ("curl", "wget")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?:-o|-O|--output|--remote-name-all)\s+(/(?:tmp|var/tmp|dev/shm)/|=(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/))"
| extend StagedFile = extract(@"(?:-o|-O|--output)[= ]+([^\s]+)", 1, CommandLine)
| extend SourceUrl = extract(@"(https?://[^\s]+)", 1, CommandLine)
| project DeviceId, DownloadTimestamp = Timestamp, DownloaderProcessId = ProcessId, Downloader = FileName,
          DownloadCommandLine = CommandLine, StagedFile, SourceUrl, AccountName;
let ShellExec = DeviceProcess
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "ksh", "python", "perl", "php")  // keep to shells maybe
| where CommandLine matches regex @"^\s*(?:/usr/(?:local/)?bin/|/bin/)?(?:ba|da|z|k)?sh\s+/tmp/"
...
```

Note interesting: the /tmp/stage2 file created by wget isn't in DeviceFileEvents sample (only 2 rows shown, maybe more). Let me check full DeviceFileEvents.

Now build the KQL detection query. Design:

```kql
// Download-and-Execute: curl/wget staging a script in /tmp followed by shell execution
let DownloadToStaging = DeviceProcess
| where FileName in~ ("curl", "wget")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?:-o|-O|--output|--remote-name-all)\s+(/(?:tmp|var/tmp|dev/shm)/|=(?:/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/))"
| extend StagedFile = extract(@"(?:-o|-O|--output)[= ]+([^\s]+)", 1, CommandLine)
| extend SourceUrl = extract(@"(https?://[^\s]+)", 1, CommandLine)
| project DeviceId, DownloadTimestamp = Timestamp, DownloaderProcessId = ProcessId, Downloader = FileName,
          DownloadCommandLine = CommandLine, StagedFile, SourceUrl, AccountName;
let ShellExec = DeviceProcess
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "ksh", "python", "perl", "php")  // keep to shells maybe
| where CommandLine matches regex @"^\s*(?:/usr/(?:local/)?bin/|/bin/)?(?:ba|da|z|k)?sh\s+/tmp/"
...
```

Hmm — keep the query focused: shells executing files from world-writable dirs.

Then:
```
ShellExec
| join kind=inner (DownloadToStaging | project-away AccountName?) on DeviceId
| where DownloadTimestamp between (ExecTimestamp .. (-Window)) ... 
```
Actually `where Timestamp between (download_ts .. execute_ts)`? Simpler: `where ExecTimestamp > DownloadTimestamp and ExecTimestamp - DownloadTimestamp <= 5m`.

Also match on staged filename equality (or parent process id link). Let's include an OR for parent-child linkage: `DownloadCommandLine == InitiatingProcessCommandLine`.

Hmm, but a join with OR conditions is fine.

Also I want results to include the direct parent-child case reliably. In the data: bash's InitiatingProcessCommandLine == curl's CommandLine exactly. So join on DeviceId AND InitiatingProcessCommandLine == DownloadCommandLine is the most reliable; plus general staged-path match for cases where parent isn't curl.
